name: Neozapatismo
summary: Neozapatismo is the political outlook of the Zapatista Army of National Liberation and its Maya base communities in Chiapas, blending Marxist influence, indigenous Maya practice and the legacy of Emiliano Zapata. It is anti-capitalist and anti-neoliberal, defends indigenous autonomy and land held by those who work it, and governs through community assemblies on the principle of commanding by obeying. It declines to seek state power or lead from a vanguard, and since 1994 has pursued civil and peaceful rather than offensive armed struggle.
scope: The EZLN-led Zapatista movement as expressed in the Fourth (1996) and Sixth (2005) Declarations of the Lacandon Jungle, the Women's Revolutionary Law and the autonomous municipalities and Good Government Councils. It does not cover other Mexican agrarian or indigenous movements or the wider alter-globalisation movement; many questions Zapatista texts never address are marked low confidence.

sources.title: Zapatista Women's Revolutionary Law
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The ten rights of the Women's Revolutionary Law and its aims against patriarchal domination.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Sixth Declaration lists health among the demands to be written into a new constitution, and autonomous communities run their own clinics; the demand is for guaranteed care, though built from below rather than by the state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The declaration condemns maquiladora labor and low pay, so higher wages fit, but the movement does not campaign on state wage policy and mostly avoids reformist demands.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Sixth Declaration describes neoliberal capitalism as commodifying people, land and culture, so a Zapatista rejects the claim that markets allocate better.

public-ownership.rationale: It opposes privatization of water, electricity, oil and forests, but the preferred ideal is community control rather than ownership by the Mexican state, which it calls illegitimate.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Anti-wealth rhetoric makes it agreeable in principle, but taxation by a state it does not recognise is not a stated Zapatista program.

unions-good.rationale: The declaration pledges support to workers' mobilizations and seeks alliance with workers and other left organisations, though it distrusts bureaucratic organisations.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Revolutionary Agrarian Law holds that land belongs to those who work it, and Zapatista schools question private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents want corporate power ended or bypassed, not regulated by a state they consider captured; this reformist framing does not fit.

cut-welfare.rationale: Hunger, health and housing are central grievances and the movement demands guaranteed provision, so cutting welfare is firmly opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Land and means of production are to be recovered by those who work them, and Zapatista communities run collective cooperatives.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The movement is a target of state surveillance and military harassment and distrusts the state, so it would reject this trade-off; inferred, not stated.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Zapatista territory bans drug trafficking and alcohol, so an adherent would not call for legal recreational drugs, though they do not argue the issue in policy terms.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The sources say nothing on speech law; adherents oppose racism strongly but also distrust a state they call illegitimate to police speech, so they split.

strong-leader.rationale: The principle of governing by obeying and rejecting top-down leaders makes a strong leader above gridlock directly contrary to the ideology.

state-harmful.rationale: The Zapatistas refuse to seek state power and build parallel self-government, but they demand a new constitution and do not call for abolishing the state outright.

limit-guns.rationale: The movement is itself armed and opposes army abuses; there is no stated stance on civilian gun control.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Fourth Declaration calls the army an occupying force and the government criminal; more police and military power is rejected.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Women's Law stresses freedom from coercion and fair work, but no source states a view on sex work, so this is left split.

decide-locally.rationale: Autonomous municipalities and Good Government Councils embody local self-governance, and authority rests with the community.

rehabilitation.rationale: Zapatista autonomous justice favors community reconciliation and work over prison, but this is inferred from practice more than declared.

traditional-family.rationale: The Women's Revolutionary Law challenges traditional patriarchal domination, including forced marriage, though communities retain family-centered life.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: No source gives a Zapatista position on same-sex marriage, and the movement's rural communities are reported to hold mixed views, so it is left split.

abortion-legal.rationale: The Women's Law grants the right to decide the number of children but does not address abortion, and communities differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement is officially secular despite liberation-theology roots among its base, and does not seek a larger public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The fight against 500 years of dispossession of indigenous peoples is the movement's founding cause.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The movement fights patriarchal domination but does not state a theory of gender; adherents' views are not documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Fourth Declaration defends indigenous history and language and the homeland, but against a national culture imposed by the powerful; the statement is ambiguous for them.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement launched an uprising and calls for a new constitution and a new world, though it now acts peacefully; it does not respect established institutions as such.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalist and solidaristic, it would not back restricting immigration; inferred, not stated.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposed to neoliberal global governance and institutions like those behind NAFTA, but favors international solidarity from below rather than top-down bodies.

free-trade.rationale: The uprising began on the day NAFTA took effect and the movement is explicitly anti-neoliberal.

nation-first.rationale: The movement seeks internationalism and solidarity among peoples, though it also defends national sovereignty against foreign capital.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: It opposes US domination and imperial power, so military intervention is distrusted; not stated directly.

open-borders.rationale: Its internationalism and solidarity with all the exploited point this way, but the sources do not address borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Concepts like lekil kuxlejal and buen vivir criticise extractivism, but no stance on limiting growth is stated.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: It defends land, forests and water against commodification, which implies support, but climate policy is not a Zapatista theme in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Its critique of commodification and its Maya-rooted worldview favor skepticism of techno-optimism; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Opposition to large corporate projects and to privatised energy makes support unlikely; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The 1994 armed uprising was declared a justified rebellion against a government it called illegitimate, though the movement has since renounced offensive arms.

experts-over-public.rationale: Governance rests on community assemblies, and the maxim 'asking we walk' prioritises listening over expert or vanguard programs.

central-planning.rationale: Rejecting vanguardism and state power, the movement favors decentralised community decision-making, not a centrally planned economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cooperatives trade locally and the movement is anticapitalist, but it has not stated a view on market socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Taxation of land value is not a Zapatista topic; their land demand is that land belong to those who work it, which neither supports nor opposes such a tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Anti-wealth stance makes it plausible, but there is no stated position.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents want autonomy from a state they distrust, but also guaranteed material needs, so the answer is split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: They oppose NAFTA and defend peasant agriculture but frame it as defending communities, not national industry policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: They reject the state's neoliberal governance and prefer community self-development; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land should go to those who work it, but collectively held communal land rather than individual small holdings is the Zapatista model.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Slogan 'everything for everyone, nothing for us' and anticapitalism hint at it, but no abolition of money is stated.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banking is never discussed; their critique targets neoliberal finance generally, with no stated view on abolishing central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages contradicts the rejection of the state and of top-down organisation.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement explicitly rejected vanguardism and party leadership in favor of radical democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule contradicts command-by-obeying and community authority.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is a core demand, but they understand it as community self-rule and are skeptical of Mexican electoral democracy, so agreement is qualified.

direct-votes.rationale: Zapatista communities decide in assemblies where any issue can be raised and voted by majority.

workers-councils.rationale: Their own model is assemblies and Good Government Councils from below, similar in spirit but based on communities, not workplaces.

right-to-secede.rationale: They demand autonomy within Mexico and a new constitution rather than secession, though they assert the right to self-government.

natural-rulers.rationale: Leaders must serve, are removable and rotate, rejecting the idea of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement renounced offensive armed action in 2005 but defends the 1994 uprising as legitimate, so it does not hold violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Fourth Declaration speaks of peace as a goal and sees war as imposed by the bad government.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement is officially secular but it has no written program on church-state relations.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Official secularism and a socialist and indigenous framework contradict scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Commodification of justice contradicts their anticapitalism and their community justice system.

military-superiority.rationale: The movement criticises the army as an occupation force and an arm of the powerful.

ethnic-nation.rationale: It calls for solidarity with people of all races and languages and a Mexico of many peoples and 'a world where many worlds fit'.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist influence is central, yet it combines class with indigenous and other axes of oppression.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Its slogan 'for everyone everything' points to material equality, though not framed as a policy of equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous control of land and resources is the central demand and autonomous territories enact it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Fourth Declaration speaks of 500 years of dispossession, supporting redress, though reparations from colonial powers are not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Their internationalism is global and from below, not along religious or civilizational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Zapatista schools criticise individualism, competition and consumerism, and the motto 'nothing for us' condemns it.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Community obligation and collective agreements are central, but they also claim rights strongly.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Maya cosmology and lekil kuxlejal give nature value of its own; the sources link it to buen vivir.

limit-population.rationale: The Women's Law gives women the right to decide how many children they have, but does not support state limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: They criticise capitalist industrial globalization but do not condemn industrial civilization itself.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Disruption driven by capital runs against their communal values; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: No Zapatista source addresses bodily enhancement technology, and nothing in their principles clearly points either way.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Contradicts their reliance on assemblies and face-to-face collective decision-making.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is not discussed; the movement uses the internet for communiques and solidarity but takes no stated position on state access to it.

restore-past-order.rationale: They draw on Zapata and Maya heritage but aim to build a new world rather than restore a past order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Marcos calls zapatismo an intuition rather than ideology, but the movement adheres to strong principles; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: They favor building autonomy from below and civil resistance over parliaments, though they also pursue public dialogue and mobilise civil society.

means-match-ends.rationale: Command-by-obeying and 'asking we walk' show organising now as the society they want, and the Sixth Declaration insists on democratic internal practice.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Zapatista communities farm and run schools and clinics; no such primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rotation of community posts limits entrenched authority, but sources do not say they seek to abolish the division of labor itself.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The slogan 'for everyone everything' and demands for housing, food and health point toward distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Its anticapitalist critique of commodification and its cooperatives imply production for community needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Sixth Declaration states that capitalism rests on exploiting workers' labor.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: It rejects vanguardism and seizing power, preferring radical democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective cooperatives and communal land work exist in Zapatista areas, though family plots also exist.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: It denounces neoliberal globalisation and US domination as sources of war and dispossession, though not a formal theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement is anticapitalist and favors redistribution so it does not hold taxes are theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Communities set binding collective rules by assembly, which sits uneasily with a pure harm principle, but no source addresses it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Fourth Declaration claims rights to sovereignty and self-government for peoples and communities, so rights are not held by individuals alone.

conscription.rationale: They refuse the government's army; their own forces are voluntary, so conscription by a state would be opposed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Voice and direct participation in assemblies are central; exit is not their model.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts anti-commodification and 'the people command'.

positive-liberty.rationale: Demands for land, food, housing and education as conditions of dignity express the view that freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: The Sixth Declaration places political power in wealthy and foreign interests and the main parties, not in universities and media, so adherents would likely disagree.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The movement is founded on indigenous dignity and equality of peoples.

organic-representation.rationale: Communal assemblies resemble community representation, yet this corporatist framing is opposed to a movement rejecting hierarchy.

total-state.rationale: The movement refuses to seek state power and insists that power stay below and accountable, which is the opposite of a state directing all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Fourth Declaration speaks of the homeland recovering dignity and memory through its indigenous heart, but as plural renewal from below, not a nationalist rebirth against decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Contradicts internationalism and rejection of imperial domination.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on collective agreements, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Land is to belong to those who work it, the opposite of serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Zapatista schooling grounds knowledge in Maya history and language as against official curricula, which suggests knowledge reflects power.

universal-morality.rationale: Dignity is universal in their rhetoric, but they also emphasise many worlds and local knowledge.

single-common-good.rationale: The motto 'a world where many worlds fit' and plurality of listening reject one single good worked out by reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: They have voiced support for Palestinians; no statement on a Jewish state is given, so inferred from this.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source deals with diaspora return; their solidarity with displaced and dispossessed people could support it but this is not stated.

revive-national-language.rationale: They defend indigenous languages but not a state-imposed national language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Collective ownership and assemblies make democratic control of work organisation core.

school-vouchers.rationale: Zapatista autonomous schools are community-run; privatised school markets conflict.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed; they oppose neoliberal austerity-style policy but do not discuss deficit rules.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom as market liberty is seen as neoliberal domination.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Sixth Declaration proposes politics based on service, honesty and keeping one's word.

national-self-determination.rationale: They demand sovereignty and self-government for peoples, though they use it for indigenous peoples more than for nation-states.

force-without-un.rationale: The Sixth Declaration condemns US military and economic domination, so unilateral force by a powerful state is rejected.

reason-over-faith.rationale: They mix Marxism with Maya cosmology and liberation theology roots, rejecting a rationalist-only epistemology.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Their solidarity with all exploited peoples argues against excluding immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not stated directly; the demand that food, health and housing be guaranteed to all points against conditioning support on work.

class-collaboration.rationale: They describe capitalists as exploiters; the Sixth Declaration puts the workers' side against capital.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Federal forces' destruction of a Zapatista library and cultural hall is denounced; preserving history and memory is a core theme.

dominated-front.rationale: They support solidarity among resistance movements worldwide against neoliberalism, which includes dominated countries.

workers-nation.rationale: The Sixth Declaration seeks solidarity with workers and the excluded across Latin America, Europe, Africa and Asia, rejecting organising along national lines only.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Women's Law asserts equal leadership and military rank for women.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest-bearing lending is not discussed; their anti-capitalism and religious-secular mix leave no clear stance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Fourth Declaration demands dignity and solidarity among peoples of all races and languages, and rests on resisting racial subordination of indigenous people.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Sixth Declaration says the governments serve foreign and wealthy interests and the law favours the rich.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: It opposes privatisation of oil and natural resources and extraction in communities' land.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: They defend cultural distinctiveness against assimilationist pressure on indigenous peoples; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory of this kind has no place in their analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: They reject electoral politics generally and so do not take a side.

national-mission.rationale: The Sixth Declaration criticises US domination and favors mutual respect among peoples, so a mission to spread one's own system would be rejected.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Women's Law was written to counter patriarchal domination, and the Sixth Declaration notes disrespect for women in society and movement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Sixth Declaration calls the major parties complicit and betrayers of the San Andres Accords.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic restriction contradicts their demand for dignity for the despised and forgotten, and the Women's Law's right to decide on children.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Fourth Declaration condemns military and police persecution and criminal government, implying accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They demand housing, land, health, education and food as rights, and oppose neoliberal minimal-state policy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the demand for dignity of all peoples and their solidarity across races.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Fourth Declaration speaks of solidarity of brothers and sisters of all races and languages, and demands dignity for all.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question of socialism in one country is a debate within Marxism-Leninism that the Zapatistas do not take up.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The 500-year dispossession narrative frames colonial occupation of indigenous lands as an injustice, though settler-state theory is not elaborated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: They demand constitutional recognition of indigenous autonomy and customary law, against uniformity.

restrict-conversion.rationale: They are secular and plural, with Catholic, Protestant and other members.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The movement is secular and pluralist and does not impose religious dietary law; communities keep livestock.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Official secularism points this way, though they run their own schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: They refuse to seek state power and want power kept below and accountable, so a strengthening socialist state is contrary to their view.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Command-by-obeying means authority is legitimate only if it is exercised by the consent of the people, and the Mexican government is called illegitimate for lacking it.

trade-surplus.rationale: Opposition to NAFTA is aimed at export-driven integration harming peasants; a mercantilist aim is not theirs, though this is inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts their stance against displacement of indigenous peoples.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They ended offensive arms use but the 1994 uprising shows they do not hold an absolute principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Zapatista schools critique competition and promote solidarity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: They reject the party system, but support for state bans on parties is not stated; they are victims of state repression.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Their critique of arbitrary power by wealthy and parties and demand for accountable rulers fits republican non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: They call for a new constitution but give no institutional design, and their own model fuses assembly and council authority.

vanguard-party.rationale: Scholarly and encyclopedic accounts say neozapatismo rejected vanguardism and party leadership in favor of radical democracy and asking while walking.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Their fight is for the forgotten and for 'everyone, everything'.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; they demand housing but not through individual purchase rights.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Sixth Declaration pledges support for the mobilizations of workers and peasants, so legal limits on strikes would be opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They attribute poverty to exploitation, dispossession and neoliberal policy, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The guiding idea of 'a world where many worlds fit' affirms diversity as a basis of shared life.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rotating posts exist but selection is by community choice rather than lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Fourth Declaration condemns the government's military persecution.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not stated; the Fourth Declaration names hunger and food among core demands, which would favor action on essential prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: They rely on independent communiques and oppose top-down control.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Sixth Declaration places the army under civil leadership of communities, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; their solidarity with all the exploited across borders makes long exclusion from citizenship unlikely.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Sixth Declaration proposes politics without material gain and Zapatista authorities serve without pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: They bind authorities to collective agreements, but they reject party structures.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They oppose neoliberal supranational arrangements, but support international solidarity.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Authority resting with the community and leaders who obey the collective contradicts a head of state commanding forces and choosing ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hierarchical church governance contradicts their anti-hierarchical outlook; secular.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement is officially secular and governs through community assemblies, so rule by senior religious scholars is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: No source addresses this Leninist stance on inter-imperialist wars; they are anti-war but this specific tactic is not stated.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Fourth Declaration claims liberty of thought and condemns repression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Their rotation of posts and removable leaders contradict long incumbency.

recall-officials.rationale: The Sixth Declaration says leaders serve and can be removed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Their anti-imperialism and critique of US dominance suggest ending military alliances, but they do not state this.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing is a demand but nothing in sources addresses renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: They are an armed movement of communities yet declared themselves committed to civil, peaceful struggle.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: They live rural, communal life but do not state it as superior.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed, and Mexico is not a divided nation in the relevant sense.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not stated; the movement runs its own schools and values learning, and many supporters are intellectuals and students.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: 'A world where many worlds fit' expresses plural, non-hierarchical cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: They condemn state killing and the government's criminal violence.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Women's Law supports education and control over reproduction, and Zapatista schools teach gender equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Their schools teach local history and sciences in a secular way.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; the Women's Law protects women from abuse but takes no stance on pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; their stance of solidarity beyond borders and plural peoples makes descent-based citizenship unlikely to be favored.

minority-language-support.rationale: Zapatista schools use indigenous languages and the movement defends them.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed, and the movement has religiously mixed members, so adherents would likely be split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Communities stress collective agreements and shared norms, but also plural ways of living; no source settles it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Sixth Declaration opposes neoliberal global economic domination, and Zapatistas have long criticised foreign debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Fourth Declaration says 'true loss of national sovereignty' came through pacts with owners of money, linking independence to economic questions.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Sixth Declaration proposes writing a new constitution from a national program built by listening to ordinary people.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty is one of the named demands of the Fourth Declaration, and the movement criticises regimes that trade rights for development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: They stress solidarity among peoples and self-reliance, and are suspicious of aid that comes with conditions, so they are split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The movement criticises militarism and armed state power, so a national nuclear arsenal runs against its stance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; they reject electoral politics and want power from below rather than a stronger presidency.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not stated; independence of central banks is a neoliberal policy feature the Sixth Declaration opposes in general terms.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Concerns state territorial disputes the movement does not engage with.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land belongs to those who work it; property subordinated to community need.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union is not discussed in the sources; their critique of vanguard party rule suggests sympathy but it is not stated.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Defence of land and water against extraction implies caution.

collective-defense.rationale: They criticise military alliances implied by US domination, but have no stated position on NATO-style pacts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: They denounce army occupation of indigenous lands and uphold consent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement is secular but distrusts the state and has Catholic liberation-theology roots, so state control of clergy is not their aim.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Heads of state are not addressed; they reject the state's top-down representation.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: They denounce the army being used against its own people.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy within a nation with their own system is exactly what they demand.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not discussed; a flat tax benefits the wealthy relative to progressive tax, which conflicts with their anti-wealth stance.

character-from-environment.rationale: Their materialist approach to formation of persons suggests it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Leaders who must obey the community and can be removed contradict a ruler placed above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; humanity-scale expansion is a distant concern relative to their communal, land-based priorities.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixing rule by few and many is not discussed; they favor radical democracy from below and reject elites.

leader-cult.rationale: The movement's masked leaders say the face is anonymous and stress collective leadership.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; the Women's Law covers choice of children and protection from abuse but not custody.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine not addressed by neozapatismo, which also rejects the party seizing power.

land-redistribution.rationale: Revolutionary Agrarian Law and opposition to Article 27 reform.

refugee-return.rationale: Right to land and homes for the displaced is a Zapatista concern.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Their internationalism and 'many worlds' pluralism contradict nationality-based territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The movement is secular and pluralist with Catholic, Protestant and other members, and claims liberty of thought as a demand.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Women's Law gives women the right to choose and to be free of coercion, which contradicts legal compulsion over dress.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose neoliberal integration yet support international solidarity.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Fourth Declaration lists indigenous peoples' linked struggle but does not seek political union by kin.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Indigenous autonomy for self-governing institutions is a central demand.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: They struggle for rights where they live and call for a more just homeland.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist influence is documented, but Marcos calls zapatismo an intuition rather than an ideology and gives weight to indigenous culture and memory.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; anti-monopoly competition policy is a liberal measure while they reject capitalism as such.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose public money serving the powerful, but also corporate collapse harming workers.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; they criticise courts as favoring the rich but also demand constitutional recognition of indigenous rights against majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Women's Law grants leadership positions to women and the Sixth Declaration calls for greater participation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autonomous communities emphasise self-reliance, but opposed to closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: They oppose NAFTA and neoliberal trade outright rather than seeking standards within it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Politics of service without material gain, 'nothing for us'.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: They rejected vanguardism and the foco model, using arms to call for a civic movement.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Authority resting with the community and a rejection of top-down command makes inherited privilege contrary to the movement.

history-own-civilization.rationale: They want schooling centred on indigenous history and language, against an official national curriculum, so the statement's framing does not map cleanly.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Fourth Declaration condemns 500 years of domination of indigenous peoples by those claiming to civilise them.

patriotic-education.rationale: They criticise the flag of foreigners and the government's patriotism but teach local history.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: They demand redress of racial and ethnic exclusion, so abolishing preferences is opposed, though they do not discuss admissions policy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Sixth Declaration treats capitalism as intrinsically exploitative and destructive, so they doubt it can adapt without ending its harms.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Their anti-imperialism opposes cultivating influence over regions once ruled by empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: They seek autonomy from neoliberal globalisation but also solidarity networks worldwide and trade through cooperatives, so it is split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Sixth Declaration seeks solidarity with workers in the rich countries too, so it does not treat them as non-exploited.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal dignity of all peoples is core, so a right to refuse service on any grounds is rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: They demand a new constitution recognising indigenous and social rights, but trust assemblies over courts, so views are mixed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Their view of 500 years of dispossession suggests no binding force for treaties made without consulting peoples, though this is inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Community authorities are chosen democratically and may be removed, which is consistent with election over inheritance.

minority-veto.rationale: Zapatista decisions pass by majority in assemblies, so no individual veto exists.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Fourth Declaration appeals to Article 39 of the Constitution against rulers who betray it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Sixth Declaration says parties and legislatures are captured and seeks power from below; it is neither monarchist nor parliamentary.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Maya cosmology and the intrinsic value of nature make this plausible, but animal suffering is not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Communities raise animals for food; no source addresses welfare standards.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: They reject paternalist charity from the privileged and want justice and power exercised from below.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Sixth Declaration proposes a new politics of service and organizing, and the movement's whole project is political participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Sixth Declaration says capitalism commodifies culture and people; this statement is a candidate and the stance is inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed in this Gramscian form, though they stress ideological and cultural domination alongside force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The declaration describes neoliberal globalisation as plundering land and resources of poor countries for corporate gain.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal dignity and solidarity across peoples contradict reserving office by birth, though the sources do not discuss it.

party-own-road.rationale: Concerns relations between communist parties, which they are outside of.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Autonomous communities stress self-reliance, yet also receive international solidarity support, so adherents would not take a firm side.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Their internationalism contradicts irredentist territorial demands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: They demand autonomy and equal participation, not rule over others.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; they demand a new constitution built from below, without stating anti-fascism as a founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; they criticise both state power and capitalism and are not in either camp.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; their anti-oppression stance suggests they would reject minimising slavery, but this is inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The Fourth Declaration says the bad government wants to erase history and the people's own memory, so contested official monuments are not a priority; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; their focus is the patriarchal domination of women, with no stated view on men's disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The Women's Law targets mistreatment of women and gives no sign of treating violence as symmetric.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Indigenous forms of governance such as assemblies and councils are their own model, drawn from Maya practice.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Fourth Declaration calls the army an occupation force serving a criminal government, so a political guardian role is rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: The Women's Law asserts women's right to fair pay for their work, but domestic labor is not explicitly addressed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Governing by obeying, with accountable and removable authorities, is the Zapatistas' central principle of power.

filial-duty.rationale: Maya community life gives weight to family and elders, but Zapatista texts do not state this; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Governance runs through community assemblies and rotating Good Government Councils on the principle of commanding by obeying, not selection by exam.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The uprising began against NAFTA and neoliberalism, which fits resisting foreign takeovers, though the movement distrusts state action.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Women's Revolutionary Law gives women the right to choose their partner and be free of coercion; divorce is not mentioned, so this is inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist, anti-neoliberal stance, which rejects privatised individual provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Zapatista land demand and Zapata's legacy favour land held by those who work it and communal holdings.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: It demands democracy but rejects the state-party system and elections as a route to power, so legislative budget control is not a Zapatista concern.

single-official-language.rationale: Indigenous autonomy and cultural rights are central demands, which implies keeping indigenous languages in public life; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from land for those who work it and resistance to neoliberal foreign capital; the movement is otherwise internationalist.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement is built on indigenous resistance to racism and exclusion, so judging policies by their effects on indigenous people fits; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist critique in the Sixth Declaration, which targets commodification and the market.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The EZLN rejects seeking state power and pursues civil, peaceful struggle; no source addresses a state arming insurgents, so this is inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Fourth Declaration defends national sovereignty and self-determination and the movement is anti-imperialist; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Sixth Declaration attacks capitalism and parties as serving money and the powerful rather than the people.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The movement relies on international solidarity and is wary of state control over civil society, though sovereignty is invoked against the state.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Women's Revolutionary Law gives women the right to decide how many children they have, and the movement distrusts state steering.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from community control of territory and land for those who work it, which suggests keeping land for the community.

job-guarantee.rationale: Work and housing appear among the demands of the Fourth Declaration, though the movement builds provision from below rather than through the state.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from its critique of electoral democracy and the state, which it sees as managed by elites.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the state and its principle of commanding by obeying, under which authority is legitimate only if it serves the community.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement opposes imperial domination yet seeks international solidarity; the sources do not settle a rule on intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Zapatista texts do not address union structure; communities are organised by assembly instead.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from its inclusive indigenous and anti-racist outlook, which has no place for blaming a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Communities differ on marriage and the Women's Law gives women free choice of partner; the sources do not address legal recognition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Fourth Declaration demands democracy, liberty and justice, which implies open government, but the texts do not address records laws.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from autonomous, land-based community economies and opposition to NAFTA-style trade.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Sixth Declaration proposes horizontal networks of groups built from below, though the EZLN itself is a structured organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Fourth Declaration criticises the national state and its legal order, and the movement appeals to indigenous rights beyond national law.

religious-nation.rationale: The movement is secular and its autonomy rests on indigenous communities, not a shared religion.

missingStatements.text: Communities should govern themselves by assemblies in which leaders must obey the collective decisions and can be removed at any time.
missingStatements.rationale: Governing by obeying, with accountable and removable authorities, is the Zapatistas' central principle of power.

missingStatements.text: A political movement should refuse to seek state power and instead build self-government from below.
missingStatements.rationale: The Fourth and Sixth Declarations propose a politics that does not fight for power and builds autonomous communities.

missingStatements.text: Elections between political parties offer ordinary people no real choice.
missingStatements.rationale: The Sixth Declaration calls elections a managed process and says the major parties betrayed the San Andres Accords.

notes: The movement calls itself plural and says zapatismo is an intuition rather than a doctrine; communities differ on social questions such as same-sex marriage and abortion, which are marked split or low confidence.
